correctness.rationale: For P_{2k}, eliminating odd sites yields (bc)^{k/2}[U_k(t)+q U_{k-1}(t)] with t=(x²-a²-b-c)/(2√bc), q=√(c/b). This is a real symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem with a single negative rank-one boundary perturbation -q. Its smallest t eigenvalue crosses -1 exactly when F_k(-1)=(-1)^k[(k+1)-kq]=0, i.e. q=1+1/k; all other t-roots remain strictly in (-1,1). For t<-1 the hyperbolic equation sinh((k+1)η)/sinh(kη)=q is strictly increasing with η, and η<log q ensures a²<x²<r², hence exactly the two real symmetric gap zeros. At equality the ±r pair are edge roots. For q_k=1+γ/k the hyperbolic and trigonometric root equations converge under η=z/k, θ=w/k to z coth z=γ or w cot w=γ, yielding the stated k^-2 three-branch continuous crossover. Checked the claimed fixed-degree normalization and boundary cases, including a=0,b=c. Independent exact SymPy recurrence/Chebyshev computations for k=1..6 agree. Finite checks are not the infinite proof; the monotonicity/rank-one argument is.
